# guiltyspark

> A self-hosted AI agent that monitors Grafana Loki logs, diagnoses the root cause
> of anomalies with Codex, writes a minimal fix plus regression tests in an isolated
> clone, validates them against your test suite, and opens a pull request for human
> review. Apache-2.0, runs anywhere Docker runs, including a Raspberry Pi.

guiltyspark differs from log summarizers and alerting tools in that its output is a
pull request rather than a notification. It runs continuously, suppresses incidents it
has already ruled on, maps each incident to its source repository, and produces code
that has passed the repository's own validation before a human ever sees it.

Autonomy is per-repository and opt-in. Every target starts in `observe` mode, where
nothing is cloned and nothing is written. Code is pushed only from targets explicitly
promoted to `draft-pr` or `pr` mode, and only after path limits, change-count limits,
and required test commands pass inside a throwaway clone. Merging is always a human
action.

## Core loop

1. Query Loki for recent logs.
2. Group noisy log lines into incidents.
3. Ask Codex to explain likely bugs, misconfigurations, and improvement opportunities.
4. Store findings in SQLite so repeated noise does not alert forever.
5. Associate each incident with its configured GitHub repository target.
6. In an isolated clone, prepare a minimal fix and regression tests, enforce patch
   policy, run validation, and optionally open a pull request.

## Autonomy modes

- `observe` — Detect and diagnose only. Nothing is cloned, nothing is written. Default for every new target.
- `fix` — Writes and validates a patch in an isolated clone. Nothing leaves the clone.
- `draft-pr` — Same validation, then pushes a branch and opens a draft pull request.
- `pr` — Opens a review-ready pull request. Still ends at human approval.

## Commands

- `guiltyspark once` — Poll Loki once and analyze what is there right now.
- `guiltyspark daemon` — Run continuously, polling on an interval. The normal mode.
- `guiltyspark doctor` — Check configuration and connectivity.
- `guiltyspark dashboard` — Serve the web console on port 8343.
- `guiltyspark replay` — Re-run a captured incident against a local checkout.

## Requirements

- Docker
- A Grafana Loki instance to read logs from
- A Codex session authenticated with a ChatGPT account (no separately billed OpenAI API key)

- [README](https://github.com/bheus/guiltyspark#readme): Installation, configuration, environment variables, repository targets, deployment.
- [Quick start](https://github.com/bheus/guiltyspark#quick-start): Minimal setup, four commands.

- [Replaying a captured incident](https://github.com/bheus/guiltyspark#replaying-a-captured-incident): Rehearsing remediation against a local checkout.
- [Dashboard](https://github.com/bheus/guiltyspark#dashboard): Web console for live anomalies, silences, and remediation records.
